## 1. Smashed Avocado & Whipped Citrus Feta

A cornerstone of our morning service, this dish pairs bright, acid-forward whipped Danish feta with coarse-crushed Hass avocado, poached heritage eggs, and warm Egyptian dukkah on crusty seeded sourdough. Success on the line depends on maintaining distinct avocado texture and serving the toast immediately while the bread is hot and the eggs are glossy.

| Service Metric | Operational Standard | Station Notes |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Service Yield | 4 Standard Portions | Hot Line & Cold Larder pass |
| Prep Time | 20 minutes (advance batch) | Whipped feta & dukkah prepped at opening |
| Ticket Time | 6 minutes per order | Eggs poached to order; bread grilled live |
| Holding Target | Whipped Feta at 2–4°C | Avocado prepped per ticket; never held mashed |
{.lined}

### Ingredients & Measurements

| Ingredient | Quantity | Unit | Kitchen Preparation State |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---|
| Hass avocados (firm-ripe) | 4 | units | Halved, pitted, and peeled per order |
| Creamy Danish feta | 200 | g | Room temperature, broken into chunks |
| Whole-milk ricotta | 100 | g | Drained through cheesecloth for 30 minutes |
| Fresh lemon | 1 | unit | Fine microplane zest and 20ml strained juice |
| Thick-cut seeded sourdough | 4 | slices | 22mm uniform slices cut from fresh bakery boules |
| Pasture-raised large eggs | 8 | units | Chilled at 4°C until ready to poach |
| House hazelnut dukkah | 40 | g | Roasted hazelnut, sesame, coriander, cumin, sea salt |
| Pickled red shallots | 50 | g | Shaved paper-thin, pickled in red wine vinegar |
| Cold-pressed olive oil | 40 | ml | Extra virgin, divided (grill brush and finishing drizzle) |
{.lined}

### Step-by-Step Method & Service Assembly

1. *Whipped Citrus Feta Base:* Place Danish feta, drained ricotta, lemon zest, 15ml olive oil, and a pinch of cracked white pepper into the food processor. Whip on high for 2 minutes until glossy, light, and completely lump-free. Transfer to a 1/6 gastronorm container; seal and hold at 3°C.
2. *Avocado Preparation:* For each ticket, scoop one avocado into a chilled stainless bowl. Add 5ml fresh lemon juice, 1g sea salt flakes, and cracked black pepper. Crush coarsely using a pastry cutter or fork, maintaining distinct 1cm chunks rather than a smooth purée.
3. *Sourdough Toasting:* Brush both sides of sourdough slices with olive oil. Place onto a preheated ribbed plancha at 220°C for 90 seconds per side until deep char marks form while the crumb remains tender.
4. *Egg Poaching:* Drop fresh eggs into gently simmering water (88°C) seasoned with 2% unseasoned white vinegar. Poach for exactly 3 minutes to achieve set whites and a molten yolk. Remove with a slotted spoon and drain onto folded linen.
5. *Plating:* Spread 70g whipped feta edge-to-edge across each hot toast. Crown with crushed avocado. Nestle two poached eggs into the center. Scatter 12g pickled shallots, dust with 10g dukkah, and finish with micro herbs and cold-pressed olive oil.

### Prep & Mise en Place Checklist

- [x] **Whipped Citrus Feta:** Whip 1.2kg morning batch by 06:30; date, label, and store below 4°C (48-hour shelf life).
- [ ] **Shallot Quick-Pickle:** Maintain 500g par in squeeze bottles; discard after 5 days of refrigeration.
- [ ] **Hazelnut Dukkah:** Toast whole spices and nuts separately; coarse-grind and store in airtight dry storage.
- [ ] **Poaching Water Bath:** Fill line immersion station, adjust to 88°C, and calibrate digital timer.
- [ ] **Avocado Par Level:** Ripen 2 flats in service drawers; verify soft give at stem before rush.

> **Chef's Note & Allergens:** Contains Dairy (feta, ricotta), Eggs, Tree Nuts (hazelnuts), and Gluten (sourdough). For gluten-free tickets, substitute toasted house seed loaf and use the designated allergen toaster.

## 2. Roasted Wild Mushroom & Leek Melt

Our signature midday hot sandwich balances rich, umami-dense roasted mushrooms and melted Swiss Gruyère against the sharp bite of whole-grain truffle mustard. The mushrooms must be seared hard over high heat rather than steamed to preserve their meaty texture and prevent the sandwich from becoming waterlogged during pressing.

| Service Metric | Operational Standard | Station Notes |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Service Yield | 4 Sandwiches | Hot Line / Panini Grill station |
| Prep Time | 25 minutes (mushroom ragout) | Sauté batch prepped before 11:00 lunch rush |
| Ticket Time | 7 minutes per order | 4 minutes active pressing in clamshell grill |
| Holding Target | Sauté held hot at >63°C | Shredded Gruyère held chilled at 2–4°C |
{.lined}

### Ingredients & Measurements

| Ingredient | Quantity | Unit | Kitchen Preparation State |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---|
| Wild mushroom medley | 600 | g | Cremini, oyster, and shiitake, cleaned and hand-torn |
| Leeks (white and pale green) | 2 | units | Halved lengthwise, rinsed clean, and finely sliced |
| Unsalted European butter | 80 | g | 40g for sauté pan; 40g softened for sandwich exterior |
| Fresh garden thyme | 15 | g | Leaves stripped from stems and roughly chopped |
| Garlic cloves | 4 | units | Microplaned into fine garlic paste |
| Aged Swiss Gruyère | 240 | g | Coarsely grated (60g allocated per sandwich) |
| Country white sourdough | 8 | slices | Uniform 18mm slices cut from artisan batard |
| Whole-grain truffle mustard | 60 | g | Dijon mustard blended with grain mustard and truffle oil |
| Flaky sea salt & pepper | 8 | g | Pre-mixed 3:1 sea salt to coarse black pepper |
{.lined}

### Step-by-Step Method & Service Assembly

1. *Mushroom Ragout Sauté:* Set a large cast-iron skillet over high heat with 15ml olive oil and 40g butter. Add sliced leeks and sauté for 3 minutes until softened. Add torn mushrooms and spread into an even single layer; cook undisturbed for 3 minutes to develop caramelisation. Toss, add garlic, thyme, salt, and pepper, and sauté for another 4 minutes until juices evaporate and edges crisp. Transfer to a steam well at 65°C.
2. *Mustard Application:* Lay out eight sourdough slices in matching pairs on the prep board. Spread 15g truffle mustard evenly across the interior face of all slices.
3. *Layering the Melt:* Distribute 30g grated Gruyère across each bottom slice. Mound 120g hot mushroom-leek ragout over the cheese base, then cover with another 30g Gruyère. Cap with the top bread slice.
4. *Grill & Press:* Generously butter the top and bottom exteriors of each sandwich with softened butter. Place into a commercial ribbed sandwich press preheated to 190°C. Lower the top plate with medium counterweight pressure; press for 4 minutes until the bread is golden-brown and the cheese is fully melted.
5. *Plating & Service:* Remove with a bench spatula, cut cleanly on a 45-degree bias, and serve with sweet cornichons and dressed rocket leaves.

### Prep & Mise en Place Checklist

- [x] **Mushroom Ragout:** Sauté 2.4kg batch at 10:30; log holding temperature hourly in the hot-line HACCP register.
- [ ] **Gruyère Portioning:** Grate 2kg block through the 6mm food processor disk; portion into 60g ramekins or pans.
- [ ] **Truffle Mustard:** Whisk 300g Dijon, 100g seeded grain mustard, and 25ml white truffle oil; bottle and chill.
- [ ] **Panini Press Seasoning:** Scrape plates clean with brass brush, apply thin vegetable oil film, and set dial to 190°C.
- [ ] **Bread Station:** Cut 40 slices of sourdough batard; stack in plastic lidded bins to prevent drying.

> **Chef's Note & Allergens:** Contains Dairy (butter, cheese) and Gluten (sourdough). Vegetarians can consume as written. For allium-free tickets, sauté sliced mushrooms to order with butter and thyme, omitting leeks and garlic.

## 3. Cardamom Brown Butter Morning Buns

Baked fresh every morning before the cafe doors open, these morning buns feature enriched brioche rolled with nutty browned butter, dark muscovado sugar, and freshly cracked green cardamom seeds. Dipping the buns in orange-blossom glaze immediately out of the oven seals moisture into the crumb while creating a delicate, crackled sugar crust.

| Service Metric | Operational Standard | Station Notes |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Batch Yield | 12 Jumbo Buns | Bakery station & pastry display pass |
| Bake Time | 22 minutes at 185°C | Baked at 06:15; second batch at 10:15 |
| Proofing Window | 75 minutes at 26°C | 80% relative humidity in proofer cabinet |
| Display Shelf Life | 8 hours at ambient room temp | Unsold stock repurposed into bread pudding |
{.lined}

### Ingredients & Measurements

| Ingredient | Quantity | Unit | Kitchen Preparation State |
|:---|:---:|:---:|:---|
| High-protein baker's flour | 500 | g | 12.5% protein bread flour, sifted |
| Whole milk | 180 | ml | Warmed to 32°C for yeast activation |
| Instant dry baker's yeast | 7 | g | Checked for active vitality |
| Caster sugar & honey | 70 | g | 50g fine caster sugar, 20g raw honey |
| Whole pasture eggs | 2 | units | Room temperature, lightly beaten |
| Unsalted butter (dough) | 120 | g | Cubed, softened to 18°C |
| Browned butter (filling) | 110 | g | Cooked to dark hazelnut foam, chilled to spreadable paste |
| Dark muscovado sugar | 130 | g | Sifted to break up lumps |
| Green cardamom seeds | 12 | g | Freshly cracked in stone mortar; coarse grind |
| Orange vanilla glaze | 120 | ml | Fresh orange juice, fine zest, and pure icing sugar |
{.lined}

### Step-by-Step Method & Service Assembly

1. *Brioche Dough Mix:* Combine flour, yeast, warm milk, sugar, honey, and beaten eggs in a spiral mixer bowl. Mix on speed 1 for 4 minutes until hydrated. Switch to speed 2 and add softened cubed butter in three additions over 6 minutes. Knead for 8 minutes until a smooth, translucent windowpane forms. Proof at room temperature for 1 hour, punch down, and retard in the chiller at 2°C for 4 hours.
2. *Filling & Shaping:* Roll chilled dough on a floured marble bench to a 35x50cm rectangle (6mm thickness). Spread the chilled brown butter paste edge-to-edge. Mix muscovado sugar with cracked cardamom and sprinkle evenly across the butter layer.
3. *Roll & Portion:* Roll the dough tightly along the long edge into a uniform cylinder. Trim 1cm from ends. Using unflavoured kitchen twine, slice into 12 equal 4cm rounds. Place into heavily buttered jumbo muffin tins dusted with granulated sugar.
4. *Proofing & Baking:* Transfer tins to proofer at 26°C and 80% humidity for 75 minutes until buns double in volume and spring back slowly when poked. Bake in a deck oven at 185°C with 3 seconds of steam for 22 minutes until deep mahogany.
5. *Glazing:* Whisk 100g sifted icing sugar with 20ml fresh orange juice and grated zest. Brush warm glaze over buns immediately upon oven discharge. Cool for 10 minutes, unmold onto wire racks, and transfer to front counter display dome.

### Daily Station Prep & Kitchen Shift Checklist

| Station & Responsibility | Opening Par Level (06:00) | Midday Handover Check (11:30) | Station Sign-off |
|:---|:---|:---|:---:|
| **Bakery Counter** | 24 Buns baked & glazed | Second batch proofed / counter tidy | Completed |
| **Hot Line (Melt)** | 2.5kg Mushroom ragout prepped | Gruyère restocked; press scraped | Completed |
| **Cold Larder (Avocado)** | 1.2kg Whipped feta; shallots full | Egg bath descaled; avocado bin filled | Completed |
| **Sanitation & Coolers** | Temperature logs verified (<4°C) | Cutting boards sanitized; FIFO applied | Completed |
{.lined}

> **Daily Storage Standard:** Store baked buns under glass cloches at room temperature. Never refrigerate baked morning buns, as cold temperatures accelerate starch retrogradation and dry out the crumb. Repurpose any remaining buns after 15:30 into morning-bun bread pudding base for weekend brunch.
